category_title: Students with non-compliant behavior and difficulty accepting instructions or consequences
student_description: Garth is an 11-year-old student who exhibits severe non-compliance, verbal outbursts, and property destruction when given direct instructions, consequences, or single teacher-selected assignments. The evidence reveals he uniquely requires high autonomy through task menus and the ability to switch tasks, alongside frequent positive adult attention and structured self-monitoring to maintain appropriate behavior.

criteria.rationale: Garth exhibits severe non-compliance and property destruction when forced into a single teacher-selected assignment, but responds well to having choices.
criteria.check: The tutor presents a menu of multiple task options for the student to choose from instead of assigning a single mandatory task.

criteria.rationale: Being locked into a task triggers Garth's defiance; knowing he has the flexibility to switch tasks reduces undesirable behavior.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly gives the student the option to change tasks or switch activities at any time during the session.

criteria.rationale: Garth requires high rates of adult attention during independent work to maintain engagement and prevent off-task behavior.
criteria.check: The tutor provides proactive attention, praise, or conversational check-ins rather than only interacting to issue directives or correct behavior.

criteria.criterion_name: Avoidance of Ultimatums and Rigid Demands
criteria.rationale: Direct commands and threats of consequences reliably trigger Garth's verbal abuse and property destruction.
criteria.check: The tutor avoids using rigid demands, forced compliance, or threats of consequences to manage the student's behavior.
